title: Strict coefficient augmentation and homotopical reduction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $O$ and $B_n$, $n\geq1$, sheaves of commutative rings, and $p_n:O\to B_n$, $q_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ ring-sheaf maps with $q_np_{n+1}=p_n$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their cochain complexes and derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and strict inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $\mathcal K$ be the full category of K-flat complexes of $O$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(O)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(O))$ and $Q_t:K(\operatorname{Tow}(O))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(O))$ be its localization. Regard each $B_n$-module as an $O$-module along $p_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The formulas
$$R(P)_n=P\otimes_OB_n,\quad R(P)_{n+1}\to R(P)_n=1\otimes q_n,\quad R(f)_n=f\otimes1$$
using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], define a functor from $\mathcal K$ to strict tower complexes. The constant tower functor $\Delta$ has a natural strict chain augmentation $a:\Delta\to R$ whose $n$-th component is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; thus $R(f)a_P=a_{P'}\Delta f$. Both functors respect chain homotopies. If $f$ in $\mathcal K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $\Delta f$ and $R(f)$ are quasi-isomorphisms of strict tower complexes. Consequently $Q_t\Delta$, $Q_tR$ and $Q_ta$ descend to the localization of $\mathcal K$ at quasi-isomorphisms. For every additive functor $E:\operatorname{Mod}(O)\to\mathcal B$ to an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], termwise levelwise $E$ carries $\Delta P$ to $\Delta E(P)$, including identity transitions; it descends to homotopy categories and preserves shifts and cone triangles there. No flatness of $B_n$ over $O$ and no K-flatness of $R(P)_n$ over $O$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(O)$. It is abelian since the site is small. For each degree $i$, define the $O$-module $(R(P)_n)^i=P^i\otimes_OB_n$ by scalar restriction along $p_n$, and set $d_{R(P)_n}^i=d_P^i\otimes1$. The tensor relations give $d^2=0$. The map $t_n=1\otimes q_n$ is $O$-linear because $q_np_{n+1}=p_n$, and $d t_n=t_n d$ since both composites take $x\otimes b$ to $d x\otimes q_n(b)$. Compose these adjacent transitions for all arrows of $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This gives a complex of strict towers: at degree $i$ the tower is $(P^i\otimes_OB_n,t_n)$. Define $R(f)^i_n=f^i\otimes1$; it commutes with differentials and transitions by the same formula, and preserves identities and compositions on pure tensors. All formulas are first maps of presheaves of tensors and hence induce the asserted maps of their sheafifications. The constant tower has terms $P^i$ and identity transitions, and $\Delta f$ has component $f$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), tensor and change-of-rings definitions; strict diagram assembly from the formulas

proof.text: Define $(a_P)^i_n(x)=x\otimes1$. This is $O$-linear: $(rx)\otimes1=x\otimes p_n(r)$, which is the $O$-action on $x\otimes1$. It commutes with $d$ because $d(x\otimes1)=dx\otimes1$, and with tower transitions because $q_n(1)=1$. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, both $(f^i\otimes1)(a_P)^i_n$ and $(a_{P'})^i_n f^i$ send $x$ to $f^i(x)\otimes1$. These equations hold as sheaf maps, so $a$ is a natural strict chain augmentation $\Delta\to R$. In Lean, use the proved sheaf unitor formula in def-pur-cochain-tensor-coherence-data and the tensor-map pure-section formula of lem-pur-module-tensor-generator-calculus.

source.place: Tag 03EK, tensor relations; agent verification of coefficient units and augmentation naturality

proof.text: If $f-g=d_{P'}h+h d_P$ for a degree $-1$ family $h^i:P^i\to P'^{i-1}$, use the constant family $h^i$ for $\Delta$ and the family $h^i\otimes1$ at level $n$ for $R$. The latter commutes with $1\otimes q_n$. Tensoring is additive on maps, so $(f-g)\otimes1=(d_{P'}\otimes1)(h\otimes1)+(h\otimes1)(d_P\otimes1)$. Thus these are homotopies in the category of strict towers, and both functors factor through maps modulo chain homotopy. The equations of Step 2 remain equations there. For $\mathcal K$ this means the homotopy category with its prescribed objects, not an assertion about K-flatness of the reduced complexes.

source.place: Definition definition-complexes-notation, homotopy category; direct tensor homotopy calculation

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f between resolving inputs, its cone K is acyclic. Use the proved independent-universe K-flat cone closure and acyclic K-flat tensor argument in the proof of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings (DerivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients): K is K-flat, and Tot(F tensor K) is acyclic for every F. Take F to be the underlying coefficient module B_n in degree zero. The single-degree total-tensor comparison identifies this with termwise left tensoring K by B_n. The symmetric tensor braiding identifies left and right tensoring. The additive mapping-cone comparison then identifies the resulting acyclic complex with the cone of termwise right tensoring f by B_n. The cone criterion proves that this is a quasi-isomorphism. This argument uses no flatness of B_n and works with independent site and coefficient universes.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YS; independent-universe acyclic K-flat tensor and cone helpers already proved in DerivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients.lean; degree-zero tensor and braiding comparisons.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(O)$. In the tower category, kernels and cokernels are computed levelwise. Thus the kernel of a differential, its image (the kernel of its cokernel), and the quotient defining $H^i$ are all computed levelwise: $H^i(X)_n=H^i(X_n)$, compatibly with maps. A map of tower complexes inducing isomorphisms on every $H^i$ at every level is therefore a quasi-isomorphism: the inverse of a levelwise isomorphism commutes with transitions by multiplying its naturality equation by the component inverses. Step 4 supplies this criterion for $R(f)$; for $\Delta f$, every evaluated map is $f$. Both are consequently quasi-isomorphisms of strict tower complexes.

source.place: Tag 02MZ (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian); cohomology and isomorphism criterion written out from levelwise kernels/cokernels

proof.text: Let $L:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K[W^{-1}]$ localize the chain-map category at its quasi-isomorphisms. Compose $\Delta$ and $R$ with passage to the tower homotopy category and $Q_t$, obtaining $F_\Delta,F_R:\mathcal K\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(O))$ and $\tau=Q_ta:F_\Delta\to F_R$. Step 5 says both functors invert $W$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore gives $\overline F_\Delta,\overline F_R$ with natural isomorphisms $\phi_\Delta:\overline F_\Delta L\simeq F_\Delta$ and $\phi_R:\overline F_R L\simeq F_R$. Clause (2) gives the unique descended augmentation with component $\overline a_{L(P)}=\phi_{R,P}^{-1}\tau_P\phi_{\Delta,P}$. This specifies descent even when the factorization is only up to natural isomorphism. In particular, for $w:P\to P\prime$ in $W$, naturality gives $\overline F_R(Lw)\overline a_{L(P)}=\overline a_{L(P\prime)}\overline F_\Delta(Lw)$. Both functor images of $Lw$ are invertible, so multiplying by their inverses gives $\overline F_R(Lw)^{-1}\overline a_{L(P\prime)}=\overline a_{L(P)}\overline F_\Delta(Lw)^{-1}$, the augmentation equation on the inverted arrows. Step 3 independently supplies homotopy descent; no claim that $R$ lands back in $\mathcal K$ is involved.

source.place: Tags 04VG/04VK, localization universal property; natural-transformation clause as stated in the cited node (Mathlib Localization.liftNatTrans)

proof.text: For the asserted additive functor $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, apply $E$ to every degree, differential and transition of a tower complex. The relations $E(0)=0$ and $E(uv)=E(u)E(v)$ make this a tower complex and functor. In a constant tower the transitions remain $E(1)=1$, giving $E(\Delta P)=\Delta E(P)$ with their chain maps. Applying $E$ to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives $E(f)-E(g)=E(d)E(h)+E(h)E(d)$; the image homotopy still commutes with transitions. Hence the functor descends to homotopy categories. For any integer $r$, the standard shift has terms $X^{i+r}$ and differential $(-1)^rd$; additivity gives $E((-1)^rd)=(-1)^rE(d)$, so this termwise functor preserves shifts, naturally in $X$. The constant-tower comparison is StrictReduction.constantSquare, lifted by mapHomologicalComplexCompIso; homotopy descent and CommShift are Mathlib functor constructions.

source.place: Definition definition-complexes-notation and section-cones; termwise additive functor and shift formulas

proof.text: For a strict tower chain map $u:X\to Y$, let $\iota_1,\iota_2,\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the biproduct maps of $Y^i\oplus X^{i+1}$. Applying $E$ to the equations $\pi_j\iota_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\iota_1\pi_1+\iota_2\pi_2=1$ shows that $(E(\pi_1),E(\pi_2))$ gives the canonical isomorphism $E(Y^i\oplus X^{i+1})\simeq E(Y^i)\oplus E(X^{i+1})$. In these coordinates $E$ takes the cone differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_Y&u\\0&-d_X\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ to $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}E(d_Y)&E(u)\\0&-E(d_X)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The isomorphisms commute with tower transitions, being defined by the projections. They also take the cone inclusion to the cone inclusion and its signed projection to the signed projection, so identify the image of $X\to Y\to C(u)\to X[1]$ with the cone triangle of $E(u)$ in the homotopy category. This proves the last clause using additivity alone. Apply Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.mapTrianglehIso to the additive termwise functor.
